A1.justification: Both readable 10-page PDFs describe EmoDubber and support comparison of their text, equations, Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–5. Both reference appendices and supplementary material that neither supplied PDF contains. The judgments below cover the included material; changes in those appendices cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original Chem and GRID experiments, unseen-speaker evaluations with MOS results, module ablations, and emotion-control analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, subjective, ablation and emotion-control results in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same LPA, PE, SIA and FUEC components, objectives and inference procedure. The input-video and frame-length notation edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both describe the same Chem, GRID and V2C-Animation coverage, LibriSpeech pretraining, and Emobox classifier-training data. The dubbing, unseen-speaker and emotion-transfer scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within the Chem, unseen-speaker and GRID comparisons in Tables 1, 2 and 4. Figure 5 retains GenerSpeech. The revised Speaker2Dub scores do not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: The included preprocessing, data splits, model settings, evaluation metrics and testing procedures match. Changes such as 1024 to 1,024 and 3280 to 3,280 are formatting edits, not setting changes.

E4.justification: The included PE/SIA/LPA ablations, guidance-scale sensitivity curves, emotion-quality evaluation, spectrogram examples and t-SNE comparison are retained. Changes to table highlighting do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains identical MOS estimates and plus/minus terms. Neither supplied text adds run counts, seeds, significance tests or explanations of uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 swaps Speaker2Dub's Chem Setting 1.0 LSE-C/LSE-D values from 10.56/3.76 to 3.76/10.56, reversing its reported ranking relative to EmoDubber's unchanged 8.11/6.92. Other absolute table values and plotted results match. Tables 1 and 4 remove parenthetical improvement figures.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of Equations 1–11 is retained. Replacing frame count T_v with F and distinguishing input V_l from fused feature V_f changes notation without revising definitions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: controllable emotional dubbing, improved lip synchronization and pronunciation, and positive/negative flow guidance. No core claim is added, narrowed or strengthened.

C2.justification: The included interpretations of module effectiveness, emotional generalization and preserved speech quality are unchanged, including the explanation of poorer pronunciation under strong sadness. No new limitation or applicability boundary is stated.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same architecture details, preprocessing parameters, batch sizes, guidance ranges, PyTorch implementation and RTX 4090 hardware disclosure. The project-page information and references to unavailable supplementary training details also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 53 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against earlier dubbing, flow-matching and emotional TTS methods does not change.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies video and frame-count notation, corrects the projection-layer typos, and standardizes thousands separators. The narrative and section order remain intact; later paragraphs shift through pagination.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 have larger text and spacing and omit red improvement annotations. Tables 3 and 5 correct best-value highlighting, including the ablation's lip-sync scores and emotional speech's LSE-D/WER scores. Figures retain their content, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability and internal consistency through clearer notation, larger comparison tables and corrected best-value highlighting. The Table 1 transposition also removes a conflict with the retained lip-sync ranking claim, without changing EmoDubber's scores. These are limited reporting improvements; the referenced appendices remain unavailable in both supplied PDFs.
